query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q1 fiscal 2025 growth drivers AI demand
normalized: 2025 ai center data demand drivers fiscal growth nvidia q1 revenue

output.content:
NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue reached a record **$22.6 billion in Q1 fiscal 2025** (quarter ended April 28, 2024), rising **23% sequentially** from Q4 FY2024 and **427% year over year**; it represented roughly **87%** of the company’s $26.0 billion quarterly revenue. [[1]]

**Primary growth driver: Hopper-based generative-AI compute.** NVIDIA attributed the expansion to “strong and accelerating” demand for generative-AI **training and inference** running on its Hopper platform, which included products such as H100 GPUs and Grace Hopper systems. [[1]]

**Demand broadened beyond hyperscalers.** Cloud-service providers remained important customers, but NVIDIA said generative-AI spending had expanded into consumer-internet companies, enterprises, sovereign-AI projects, automotive, and healthcare—creating several multibillion-dollar end markets rather than relying solely on a narrow group of cloud buyers. [[1]]

**AI-infrastructure buildout supported system-level sales.** NVIDIA highlighted new AI-networking offerings—Quantum and Spectrum-X800 switches—optimized for trillion-parameter GPU computing, as well as expanded AI collaborations with AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft, and Oracle. [[1]]

**Enterprise inference was becoming an additional catalyst.** The launch of NVIDIA AI Enterprise 5.0 and NIM inference microservices was intended to accelerate enterprise generative-AI application development, extending demand from model training into deploying and serving models. [[1]] 

In short, the extraordinary Q1 FY2025 Data Center growth reflected a supply-backed ramp in Hopper AI systems and an unusually broad AI-capex cycle spanning hyperscale cloud, internet platforms, enterprise deployments, sovereign infrastructure, and industry-specific customers. [[1]]

sources.title: NVIDIA Corporation - NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for First Quarter Fiscal 2025
